forecasts.reason: 12 steps × ~16 ms ≈ 0.18 s saved, the same as E041's −0.17 s. E041/E045/E053 say early steps on learning layers cost about the dial (~0.15–0.2 pp), so it lands near the break-even point and the gate is a coin flip.

Dropping Newton-Schulz plus three compiled Muon launches saves ~0.15–0.2 s. But SGD loses the fixed-norm filters and was ~0.6 pp worse in E005→E006, and a port at batch 2000 tends to lose more than the break-even 0.25 pp.

Inductor's fused GELU is mostly bytes-bound, and tanh-GELU/SiLU save the same bytes as erf-GELU (the full mask is still kept), so the gate probably fails (~55%). Then nothing is committed and ar.py reports the tip's own distribution. If it does run, expect only −1–2% time.

32 fewer steps but the same pixels: it saves only the per-step overhead plus Muon NS (~1.5–3 ms per step) and some low-res utilization, ~0.1 s. Mirroring E045's +0.135 pp, expect ~−0.1 pp. Too close to 0.15 to separate H5.1.3 from H5.2.1 cleanly.

cruxes: Is the per-step overhead (launch, Muon NS, optimizer, Lookahead) at 20/24 px large enough, ≥3 ms per step, that cutting steps with a bigger batch or by dropping Muon saves ≥0.15 s? Or is cost purely pixel-proportional, so that only pixel or step removal pays?
Is SGD at batch 2000 with the airbench normalization within 0.25 pp of Muon on this freeze-heavy recipe (PR #3 says yes, E006 says no)?
Does tanh-GELU or SiLU actually lower the fused-kernel time in Inductor's output, or is GELU's cost all bytes, so the gate fails and I097 reports the tip?
structured_output.world_model: W3 (cost lens), after E059. The tip is E049 (5.20 ±0.03 s, seeds 0–2 ≈ 0.7538 ±0.0025; population ≈ 0.7528). The remaining levers each move about 1–4% of time. Per-step costs: 16/21/26/32 ms at 20/24/28/32 px, plus about 0.25 s fixed. Accuracy follows the number of steps taken on layers that are still learning. Removing early steps costs roughly the dial rate (~0.8–1.5 s per pp). Only truncation after a layer finishes learning is close to free. When an idea is gated or diagnostic only, ar.py reports the tip's own distribution, so I forecast that rather than the hypothetical result. Muon vs SGD is the last big structural axis. My prior is that Muon's fixed-norm filters matter here, so swapping in SGD saves ~0.15–0.2 s but loses more than 0.25 pp.
